title: Instalment Buying
summary: Under an instalment scheme the buyer pays part of the price at once, takes the article home, and pays the rest in regular instalments. The price if paid fully in cash at once is the cash price. The part paid at the time of purchase is the cash down payment. The later regular payments are instalments. Because the seller waits for part of the money, the buyer pays extra — the interest charged under the instalment plan.

Balance (amount still owed) = cash price − cash down payment. Total amount paid = cash down + sum of the instalments. Interest charged = total amount paid − cash price = sum of instalments − balance. Example: a chair costs ₹2,700 cash, or ₹600 down plus 3 instalments of ₹750; total paid = 600 + 2250 = ₹2,850, interest = ₹150.
## Finding the rate of interest (simple interest)

With monthly instalments the buyer owes a different principal each month. Add these monthly principals to get the principal for one month. Example: fan ₹1,500 cash, or ₹360 down + 3 monthly instalments of ₹390. Balance = 1140; interest = 3 × 390 − 1140 = ₹30. Owed for month 1: 1140; month 2: 1140 − 390 = 750; month 3: 750 − 390 = 360; total = 2250 rupee-months. Rate: 30 = 2250 × R × 1/(100 × 12) ⇒ R = 16% p.a. With a single later payment: interest = payment − balance, and R = interest × 100/(balance × time).

If the interest rate is given and the instalment x is unknown, write the principal owed each month in terms of x (balance, balance − x, balance − 2x, …), find the interest on their total, and use: sum of instalments = balance + interest. Washing machine: ₹19,400 cash, ₹4,200 down, 3 equal monthly instalments, 16% p.a. Balance 15,200; owed 15200, 15200 − x, 15200 − 2x (total 45600 − 3x); interest = (45600 − 3x) × 16/(100 × 12) = (45600 − 3x)/75; also interest = 3x − 15200. Solving gives x = ₹5,200.

When interest is compounded, each instalment is worth less today: the balance equals the sum of the present values of the instalments. For two half-yearly instalments at 8% p.a. compounded half-yearly (4% per half year): x/1.04 + x/(1.04)² = balance.

objective: Fill in the blanks: (i) Under an instalment plan, the part paid at the time of purchase is the ____. (ii) Interest charged = sum of instalments − ____.

(i) cash down payment.
(ii) balance (= cash price − cash down), because the instalments repay the balance plus interest.
Write True or False: (i) Under an instalment plan the buyer usually pays more than the cash price. (ii) Interest under an instalment plan is charged on the full cash price for the whole period.

(i) True: the extra is interest for the delayed payment.
(ii) False: interest is charged only on the amount still owed, which falls after each instalment.

A sewing machine is sold for ₹7,500 cash down and ₹4,360 after 6 months. If interest is charged at 18% per annum, find the cash price.

Let the cash price be ₹C; balance = C − 7500.
Amount after 6 months = balance × (1 + 18 × ½/100) = 1.09 × (C − 7500).
1.09(C − 7500) = 4360 ⇒ C − 7500 = 4000 ⇒ C = ₹11,500.

or: A TV costs ₹20,000 cash or ₹5,000 down and ₹15,500 after 4 months. Find the rate of interest.

vsa: A camera is bought for ₹5,000 cash down and ₹21,000 after 3 months. If interest is 20% per annum, find the cash price.

Let the cash price be C; balance = C − 5000.
Interest for 3 months at 20% = 20 × 3/12 = 5%, so 21000 = 1.05(C − 5000).
C − 5000 = 20000 ⇒ C = ₹25,000.
A radio costs ₹1,000 cash or ₹400 down and ₹630 after 6 months. Find the rate of interest.

Balance = ₹600; interest = 630 − 600 = ₹30 for ½ year.
30 = 600 × R × ½/100 = 3R ⇒ R = 10% per annum.

la: A washing machine costs ₹15,000 cash or ₹2,250 cash down followed by two equal half-yearly instalments. If the interest charged is 8% per annum compounded half-yearly, find each instalment.

Balance = 15000 − 2250 = ₹12,750. Rate per half-year = 4%.
The balance equals the present value of the two instalments x:
x/1.04 + x/(1.04)² = 12750.
Multiply by (1.04)² = 1.0816: 1.04x + x = 12750 × 1.0816 ⇒ 2.04x = 13,790.40 ⇒ x = ₹6,760.
Each half-yearly instalment is ₹6,760.
